head: ba457bf
coverage_caveats: Python dependency tier UNSCANNED: pip-audit unprovisioned.
SEC3-003 reproduced against .claude/hooks/lib/prom-parse.js with fixtures; no 5xx-producing route exists in group A to reproduce it end to end against the live server.

The SEC3-001 cardinality bound is a property of the httptools HTTP parser, not of application code. Under 'uvicorn --http h11' arbitrary RFC 9110 token methods are accepted and B-2 re-opens as genuinely unbounded. No Dockerfile/compose exists at HEAD and deployment.md specifies no --http flag, so httptools is what production gets and is what was tested.

round2_block_disposition.claim: /metrics Prometheus exposition injection via percent-decoded scope['path']
round2_block_disposition.method: reproduction attempted and failed, plus two independent refutations
round2_block_disposition.evidence: Round-2 payload re-sent percent-encoded as the request path: forged 99999 series absent; route labels are exactly ['/health','/metrics','<unmatched>']; zero control characters other than LF in the whole exposition. Refutation 1: the only non-constant label channel is `method`, and httptools/llhttp answers 400 Bad Request to a method containing a double-quote, a backslash, CR, VT or NUL and to any valid-token-but-unknown method, so none reach scope['method']. Refutation 2: prom-parse.js splits on LF only and trims, so a CR-forged label parsed to 0 series, not 2. Impact test: slo-check.js reports {verdict:pass, error_rate_pct:0, p95_ms:4.75} after ~1700 hostile requests, versus round 2's forged 99.90%.

round2_block_disposition.claim: /metrics unbounded cardinality -> unauthenticated memory DoS (60,000 label values, +28.2 MB)
round2_block_disposition.disposition: CLOSED AS FILED; bounded residual downgraded to WARN SEC3-001
round2_block_disposition.evidence: 5,000 distinct unmatched paths on one keep-alive connection: series 135 -> 135, distinct label sets 126 -> 126, bytes 10868 -> 10882 (zero growth). The new histogram state inherits the bound: _duration_counts/_duration_totals are keyed (method, route_label(scope)) and every bucket list is allocated len(_LATENCY_BUCKETS)+1 == 12 (measured 12 vs bounds+inf 12). Residual measured: a 35-method x 7-path sweep grows the exposition to 1611 series / 1506 label sets / 130289 bytes permanently, bounded by 35 x (routes+1) x statuses.

round2_block_disposition.claim: errors.py discarded HTTPException.headers; 405 lost Allow, 401 lost WWW-Authenticate
round2_block_disposition.evidence: PROPFIND /health -> 405 Method Not Allowed with 'allow: GET'; GET /nosuch -> 404 with the envelope; both carry content-type application/json and x-request-id.

round2_block_disposition.disposition: CONFIRMED AS A DEFECT, DOWNGRADED TO WARN SEC3-002 on reachability
round2_block_disposition.method: reproduction (regex) plus refutation of reachability (caller graph and backend bound)
round2_block_disposition.evidence: Regex in isolation: 1000d 0.4ms, 2000d 1.4, 4000d 5.5, 8000d 22.9, 16000d 99.8, 32000d 410.0, 64000d 1653.1 - clean 4x per doubling, O(n^2). For the 8-byte input '1e100000': toFixed(2) = 1.23 ms, the grouping regex = 4301 ms, so evaluator 3's round-2 refutation timed the wrong sink by ~3500x and security 3's isolation was correct (4301 ms vs the reported 4152 ms). Reachability: nothing upstream bounds the digit count (toQuantizedDecimal checks only isFinite; toWire expands to 100,004 chars), but the only caller of format() is MoneyText and MoneyText has zero callers - frontend/src contains exactly two files with no entrypoint, router or fetch - and the backend cannot supply such a value (Money('1e30'), Money('1e100000') and a 100,000-literal-digit string are all rejected with the typed InvalidMoneyAmountError because Decimal.quantize exceeds the 28-digit context precision). Flips to BLOCK/high on the first commit that renders MoneyText from input the backend did not mint.

findings.description: route_label() is correctly bounded but `method` remains a free label over llhttp's ~35 accepted methods, and _request_counts/_duration_counts/_duration_totals are process-global module state that is never evicted. Measured: one anonymous sweep of 35 methods x 7 paths grew the exposition from ~10 KB to 1611 series / 1506 label sets / 130289 bytes, permanently. Ceiling is 35 x (routes+1) x statuses and scales with every route groups B-M add.
findings.fix: Allow-list the `method` label to the methods the app serves and bucket the rest as a single `<other>` value, the way route_label() already does with `<unmatched>`.
findings.evidence: measurement: 35 distinct method labels, 3 distinct route labels, 130289 exposition bytes

findings.description: Quadratic thousands-separator lookahead re-scans to end-of-string at every position: 4301 ms for the 8-byte input '1e100000' (CWE-1333). Money.fromWire bounds only isFinite(), and toWire() expands the exponent to a 100,004-character string. WARN rather than BLOCK because MoneyText is the only caller of format() and has zero callers, and the backend rejects oversized money values.
findings.fix: Use the linear form digits.replace(/\d(?=(\d{3})+$)/g, '$&,') or Intl.NumberFormat, and cap the integer-digit count in toQuantizedDecimal so fromWire has a stated precondition.
findings.evidence: reproduction: quadratic scaling table 1000d 0.4ms -> 64000d 1653.1ms; sink split toFixed 1.23 ms vs regex 4301 ms

findings.description: Anonymous, unthrottled request volume dilutes the SLO signal and masks a real outage. errorRate() is 5xx over all lifetime http_requests_total and histogramP95() aggregates across every label set; counters are cumulative-since-boot and never reset. Reproduced against prom-parse.js: a genuine 50.00% error rate is masked to 0.0100% (under the 1% budget, so it PASSES) by 1e6 anonymous 404s, and a genuine 9525 ms p95 is masked to 4.8 ms (budget 500, PASSES). One flood poisons both ratios for the process lifetime. This is the volume half of the threat B-1 was the injection half of.
findings.fix: Have the sensor exclude the route=<unmatched> label (the product already emits it) and compute a windowed rate rather than a lifetime ratio; authenticate /metrics with E1-S1.

findings.description: Redaction is byte-shape based and is defeated by formatting. Measured with 123456789012 and ABCDE1234F registered - redacted: plain, spaced, dash-separated up to 4, lowercase PAN, spaced PAN, NFKD form. NOT redacted: dot, underscore and slash separators, NBSP U+00A0, soft hyphen U+00AD, zero-width space U+200B, fullwidth digits U+FF10-FF19, dotted PAN, and any separator run longer than 4. Live impact is nil today: there are zero register_sensitive/redact_values call sites in backend/src (ba457bf added them to specs/bundles, not to code). Severity rises to high the moment E1-S1 or E4-S1 lands a real call site.
findings.fix: NFKC-normalise and strip Unicode Cf/Pd/Zs categories from both haystack and needle before matching, instead of enumerating separator characters.
findings.evidence: measurement: 7 of 12 formatting variants bypass redaction; grep confirms 0 production call sites

findings.description: The lru_cache(maxsize=256) on _redaction_pattern retains the raw PII value as the cache KEY for the process lifetime. Proven: after end_redaction_scope(), _redaction_pattern(AADHAAR) is served from cache (hits 0->1, misses unchanged at 1) and the retained compiled pattern still embeds the value. Up to 256 applicants' PAN/Aadhaar survive request teardown in process memory, visible in any core dump, and shared across users.
findings.fix: Drop the cache, or key it on a salted digest and never retain the plaintext.
findings.evidence: measurement: cache_info hits 0->1 with misses static across a scope teardown; pattern string contains the value

findings.description: X-Request-ID is accepted unvalidated and unbounded. Measured: a 100,000-byte header returns 200 OK, is echoed in the response header (100,014 bytes) and is written verbatim to the access log as a single 100,146-byte JSON line; a PAN-format id 4111111111111111 is logged unredacted because redaction covers only registered values. Explicitly refuted: no CRLF response-header injection - bare LF and bare CR in the value are rejected at the parser with 400, and a CRLF-embedded value is ordinary request-header framing.
findings.fix: Accept the inbound id only when it matches ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$; otherwise generate one.
findings.evidence: measurement: 200 OK, 100014-byte echoed header, 100146-byte log line, PAN id present in log

findings.description: Host-header-reflected open redirect. Reproduced: GET /health/ with a Host header of evil.example returns 307 with a Location pointing at http://evil.example/health, because Starlette's redirect_slashes builds the URL from the request URL, which is built from the Host header. Material behind a shared cache or CDN, and a credential-theft path as soon as a story generates a reset or callback link from the request URL.
findings.fix: Add TrustedHostMiddleware with an explicit allowed_hosts allow-list in build_fastapi_app, and configure the deployed base URL rather than deriving it from the request.
findings.evidence: reproduction: 307 Temporary Redirect with an attacker-chosen Location host

findings.description: No Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options or Strict-Transport-Security on any response, including the /docs Swagger UI HTML - the one HTML surface served, and therefore the one that is framable and MIME-sniffable.
findings.fix: Add a small ASGI middleware setting X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, a default-deny CSP, and HSTS behind TLS.
findings.evidence: measurement: none of the four headers present on any probed response

findings.description: /docs and /openapi.json both return 200 with no authentication. Harmless content today (two operational endpoints), but this is the document E1-S2-AC3 enumerates the guarded routes from, so from group B onward it is a complete machine-readable attack-surface map - including the request-body schemas a807678 just made it emit correctly.
findings.fix: Set docs_url/redoc_url/openapi_url to None outside development, or guard them with the auth dependency arriving in E1-S1.
findings.evidence: measurement: GET /docs -> 200, GET /openapi.json -> 200, no auth challenge

findings.description: The _MAX_CONTEXT_VALUE_CHARS = 200 cap sits inside the isinstance(value, str) branch, so it does not apply to non-string scalars. Measured: a 5000-character string is correctly dropped but a 4000-digit int egresses whole (4020 bytes of context on the wire). Second-order: for an int above sys.get_int_max_str_digits() (4300, reachable by arithmetic such as 10**5000), str(value) raises ValueError inside _sanitise_value - i.e. inside the exception handler - turning a typed 4xx into an unhandled 500. Latent: zero production AppError subclasses or raisers.
findings.fix: Apply the length cap to the rendered text of every scalar before scrubbing, and guard the str(value) conversion so a pathological value is dropped rather than crashing the handler.
findings.evidence: measurement: 5000-char str dropped; 4000-digit int present with 4000 digits, 4020 wire bytes

findings.description: Money.multiply lets a bare decimal.Overflow escape the typed-error contract: multiplying by Decimal('1e1000000') raises decimal.Overflow, which derives from ArithmeticError and not from InvalidOperation, so neither except clause (lines 63, 75) catches it, and the class docstring's promise of InvalidMoneyAmountError is broken. Result is a 500 where the contract specifies 422. Round-2 timing dispute SETTLED: the measured cost is 0.0 ms, so neither 9708 ms (eval-3) nor 109 ms (sec-3) is right and there is NO DoS; the 387 ms measured for 10**200000 is big-integer construction in the harness and that path raises the typed error correctly. No information leak, since handle_unexpected returns a fixed message.
findings.fix: Catch decimal.DecimalException (or ArithmeticError) in __init__ and _quantize instead of InvalidOperation alone.
findings.evidence: measurement: 1e1000000 -> decimal.Overflow leaked in 0.0 ms; 1e100000 and 10**40 -> typed error

findings.description: _LABEL_ESCAPES escapes backslash, double-quote and newline only - carriage return and every other C0 character are unescaped. Unreachable at HEAD: no attacker-controlled channel can carry them (see B-1), and prom-parse.js splits on LF only so a CR could not forge a series even if it arrived. Recorded as defense in depth against a future label channel.
findings.fix: Add CR to the table and hex-escape or reject any remaining C0/C1 character plus U+2028/U+2029 in _escape_label.
findings.evidence: refutation: CR payload parsed to 0 series by prom-parse.js; CR in the method token answered 400 by httptools

findings.description: Absolute filesystem paths still egress through the error envelope's context. Measured: a context value holding an absolute Windows path to a private-key file passed through unchanged; _CREDENTIAL_URI correctly drops a database URI carrying inline credentials, but there is no path filter. Round 2's claim still holds; latent because nothing raises AppError in production yet.
findings.fix: Drop values matching an absolute-path shape (drive-letter prefix, leading slash, or UNC prefix) as well as credential URIs.
findings.evidence: measurement: path value unchanged in sanitise_context output

findings.description: observe_duration validates none of its input: nan, inf and negative durations are all accepted; nan is mis-bucketed into +Inf and renders the histogram sum as nan, which would make a scraper drop the series. Not attacker-reachable - the only caller passes a monotonic time.perf_counter() delta. The strict zip in the exposition renderer cannot raise: measured 12 bounds against 12-element counts lists, structurally guaranteed by the [0] * (len(_LATENCY_BUCKETS) + 1) allocation.
findings.fix: Ignore any seconds value that is not finite and non-negative.
findings.evidence: refutation: _histogram_lines() rendered 16 lines without raising even with nan/inf forced into the state

findings.description: HEAD /health returns 405. RFC 9110 section 9.3.2 requires HEAD wherever GET is supported, so a container or load-balancer probe configured for HEAD marks the service unhealthy. Availability-adjacent rather than a vulnerability; noted because /health is the group-A contract surface.
findings.fix: Declare the route with methods GET and HEAD via router.api_route.
findings.evidence: measurement: HEAD /health -> 405 Method Not Allowed, allow: GET

findings.description: /metrics has no authentication. Judging the deferral rather than the absence, as instructed: E15-S4 Scope Out defers auth to an api-contracts.md amendment plus the auth layer arriving with E1-S1 (group B), and the exposition today carries only request counts, route templates and latencies for two operational endpoints - no PII, no secrets, no version information beyond what /health already returns publicly. The deferral is ACCEPTABLE for group A, conditional on closing in the same sprint as E1-S1, because SEC3-001 and SEC3-003 are only exploitable while the endpoint is anonymous.
findings.fix: Close with E1-S1 alongside the api-contracts.md amendment, as scoped.
findings.evidence: measurement: GET /metrics -> 200 with no auth challenge

findings.description: The SAST and secrets tiers are UNSCANNED, not passed: gitleaks, semgrep and pip-audit are all unprovisioned and loudly skipped, so the computational scan's 'no findings at or above high' is vacuous for those tiers. My own inferential review of the 13 changed files found no hardcoded credential pattern (string-literal assignment to password/api_key/secret/token/private_key: none) and no dangerous frontend sink (raw-HTML injection props, innerHTML, eval, new Function: none), but that is a 13-file diff review, not a repository-wide secrets scan.
findings.fix: Provision gitleaks, semgrep and pip-audit before the next gate round, or record an explicit sensor waiver naming the uncovered tiers.
findings.evidence: grep over the changed set returned no matches for either pattern family

findings.description: npm audit reports 1 critical (vitest) + 1 high (vite) + 3 moderate, all devDependencies, absent from any production image. No production dependency is affected (decimal.js 10.6.0, react, react-dom). Now genuinely auditable because frontend/package-lock.json and backend/uv.lock are both committed as of round 3.
findings.fix: Bump on the next dependency-maintenance pass; not a merge blocker.
findings.evidence: gate-lead npm audit result, corroborated by reading the package.json dependency/devDependency split
